data.title: Optimal Defensive Position
data.solution:
n = int(input())
grid = [input().split() for i in range(n)]

#find pieces
pieces = []
for row in range(n):
    for col in range(n):
        if grid[row][col]=='X': pieces += [[row,col]]

#find intersecting cells
cell1 = grid[pieces[0][0]][pieces[1][1]]
cell2 = grid[pieces[1][0]][pieces[0][1]]

print(cell1 if int(cell1)>int(cell2) else cell2)
data.statement:
On a tic-tac-toe board of size [[n]], two opposing players have each placed a piece, marked with an {{X}}. Neither piece shares a row or a column. The best move in this circumstance is always to place the next piece on one of the two tiles that shares a row with one piece and a column with the other.
The tiles on the board each have their own value, from 1 to [[n]]^2, representing their priority (higher value = higher priority). Tiles that contain pieces will show {{X}} instead of their priority value regardless of the owner. The owner of each piece is irrelevant.

With this information, find the best tile on which to place the next piece, tie breaking based on priority, and return the priority value for that tile.

Note: The given tile priorities are consistent between tests for each size but are not necessarily meaningful outside of the context of this puzzle.
data.constraints:
3<=[[n]]<=9
1<=tile value<=[[n]]^2 <<or>> tile value={{X}}
All tile priority values will be distinct.
The board will always be given with exactly two pieces placed in differing rows and columns.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

On a tic-tac-toe board of size n, two opposing players have each placed a piece, marked with an X. Neither piece shares a row or a column. The best move in this circumstance is always to place the next piece on one of the two tiles that shares a row with one piece and a column with the other.
The tiles on the board each have their own value, from 1 to n^2, representing their priority (higher value = higher priority). Tiles that contain pieces will show X instead of their priority value regardless of the owner. The owner of each piece is irrelevant.

With this information, find the best tile on which to place the next piece, tie breaking based on priority, and return the priority value for that tile.

Note: The given tile priorities are consistent between tests for each size but are not necessarily meaningful outside of the context of this puzzle.
Input
Line 1: An integer n for the width and height of the board
Next n Lines: n space-separated values representing the tiles in each row. Each value is either the tile priority value or X if the tile is occupied
Output
1 Line: The priority value of the tile on which the next piece should be placed.
Constraints
3<=n<=9
1<=tile value<=n^2 or tile value=X
All tile priority values will be distinct.
The board will always be given with exactly two pieces placed in differing rows and columns.
Example
Input
3
8 4 7
X 9 2
6 X 5
Output
9
